Regular Council Meeting CITY OF SOLANA BEACH
ACTION AGENDA
The Action Agenda of the City Council Meeting is a document provided immediately following the Council Meeting in order for staff and the public to be aware of the business transacted and actions taken by Council. This is a preliminary draft and not a public record. The meeting's legal record is the Minutes approved by the City Council.
SOLANA BEACH CITY COUNCIL
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY and PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY
JOINT
REGULAR
MEETING

06:00 P.M.
CITY COUNCIL CHAMBERS
635 S. HIGHWAY 101
SOLANA BEACH, CALIFORNIA
The City Council acts as the City of Solana Beach Redevelopment Agency and the Public Financing Authority.
NOTICE
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, persons with a disability may request an agenda in appropriate alternative formats as required by Section 202 of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990. Any person with a disability who requires a modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should direct such request to the City Clerk's office at (858) 720-2400 at least 48 hours before the meeting.
As a courtesy to all meeting attendees, please set cellular phones and pagers to silent mode and engage in conversations outside the Council Chambers.
The Regular Meetings of the City Council are scheduled for 2nd and 4th Wednesdays and are broadcast live on Cox Communications, Channel 19, and Time Warner, Channel 24.
A full City Council agenda packet with all backup information is available at City Hall and the Solana Beach branch of the San Diego County Library the Friday before each Council meeting and on the web at www.ci.solana-beach.ca.us .

Regular Council Meeting SOLANA BEACH CITY COUNCIL
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY AND PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY
JOINT REGULAR MEETING
MINUTES
WEDNESDAY, APRIL 25, 2007
06:00 P.M.
CITY COUNCIL CHAMBERS
635 S. HIGHWAY 101,
SOLANA BEACH, CALIFORNIA
The City Council acts as the City of Solana Beach Redevelopment Agency and the Public Financing Authority.
CALL TO ORDER AND ROLL CALL:
Present:
Heebner, Kellejian, Roberts, Nichols, and Campbell.
Absent:
None.
Also Present:
David Ott, City Manager
James Lough, City Attorney
Leticia Rodriguez, Deputy City Clerk
Chandra Collure, City Engineer
Dennis Coleman, Finance Dir.
Steve Didier, Management Analyst
Mary Blais, Interim Community Development Dir.
Mayor Heebner called the meeting to order at 6:05 p.m.
FLAG SALUTE:
Leslea Meyerhoff, Consultant, led the flag salute.
APPROVAL OF AGENDA:
MOTION: Moved by Roberts and seconded by Nichols to approve the agenda Motion carried unanimously.
PROCLAMATIONS:
Bike to Work Day – May 18, 2007
Mayor Heebner read the proclamation for Bike to Work Day.
ORAL COMMUNICATIONS:
Ariana Ayazi stated that she is the Center Director at St. Leos Headstart. She said that there are concerns that traffic on Genevieve is dangerous and cars travel at excess speeds. She stated that there should be a speed bump or stop sign before approaching Ida Avenue.
Council requested that the City Manager provide an update of this issue and report back to the Community. David Ott, City Manager, stated that this issue is currently being looked at and will be taken to the Ad-Hoc committee.
Don Rodmel stated that he lives on Genevieve and stated that there are problems with speeding on this street. He requested that a speed bump be placed put on this street and is concerned for safety of the children that go to the nearby school.
Policewatch.org stated that he wanted to speak about three initatives regarding police brutality in the state, that the initiatives would require all audio and video recording of all police contacts, and that a copy of the petetition can be obtained at finishfirstinc.com.
Dr. Ed Siegel said that the City Song was heard around the world on his travels. He said he missed the public hearings on Cedros Crossing, that he does not support the massive structure obscuring the City, urged Council to take time in making a decision on the Cedros Crossing project, and stated that it would change the character of the City.
Molly Gillies said that she attends Skyline School and suggested that there be one day designated out of the year when no vehicles are allowed on the roads except for emergency vehicles and that people would be able to walk in the roads without worrying about cars or safety issues.
COMMUNITY ANNOUNCEMENTS:
Mayor Heebner stated that there would be a neighborhood forum to discuss Sheriff department services April 26th at 6:00 p.m.
Councilmember Roberts stated that the San Dieguito Alliance for Drug Free Youth will be having their networking lunch this week, May 1st is the Friends Night Out at the Solana Beach Library, NCTD will be having free Senior's Bus Day on May 4th, May 11th would be the Chamber and Commerce meeting at the Fletcher Cove Community Center, San Eljio Lagoon Day is on May 12th, May 19th is San Dieguito Heritage Day barbecue, and May 17th is the Solana Beach Arts Alive Banner Program.
Deputy Mayor Kellejian said that on May 2nd will attend the next Solana Beach Chamber of Commerce Sundowner.
COMMENTARY:
Deputy Mayor Kellejian stated that Jerri Finell Mayor of Del Mar has resigned and requested that a card be sent from the Council and the community.
Councilmember Roberts stated that the Civic and Historic Society had requested that Council assist in saving the Mormon Chapel on Granados Ave. but have since withdrawn their request and they would look into other structures in the City that have historic value so they may be preserved. He announced that the Solana Beach Ball was held to benefit education and was successful.
CONSENT CALENDAR: (Action Items) (Items 1-5)
Items listed on the Consent Calendar are considered routine; however, any member of the public may address the City Council on an item of concern by submitting to the City Clerk a request to speak form before the Consent Calendar is addressed. Those items removed from the Consent Calendar by a member of the Council will be trailed to the end of the agenda, while all other Consent Calendar items removed by the public will be discussed immediately after approval of the Consent Calendar.
MOTION: Moved by Roberts and seconded by Kellejian to approve the consent calendar Motion carried unanimously.

MOTION: Moved by Roberts and seconded by Kellejian to approve Motion carried unanimously.

MOTION: Moved by Roberts and seconded by Kellejian to approve Motion carried unanimously.

Adopt Resolution 2007-039

This portion of the agenda provides citizens an opportunity to express their views on a specific issue as required by law after proper noticing by submitting a speaker slip to the City Clerk (located on the back table).  After considering all of the evidence, including written materials and oral testimony, the City Council must make a decision supported by findings and the findings must be supported by substantial evidence in the record.  An applicant or designee for a private development/business project, for which the public hearing is being held, is allotted a total of fifteen minutes to speak, as per SBMC 2.04.210.  A portion of the fifteen minutes may be saved to respond to those who speak in opposition.  All other speakers have three minutes each. Please be aware of the three-minute timer light on the Council Dais.
PRESENTATIONS:
Solana Beach Workplan 2006/07 Accomplishments - added on April 19, 2007
David Ott, City Manager, introduced the item and reported that the top six priorities of the Council workplan included, capital improvement project management, fiscal sustainability, NCTD District Site, Land Use issues - phase 2, Local Coastal Plan adoption, and master planning such as the La Colonia Master Plan Needs Assessment. He asked the City department heads to report on some highlights of accomplishments during the past year within their departments.
Mary Blais, Interim Community Development Director, stated that the Planning department had been working on the following projects over the last year which included, the Draft Land Use Plan for the Local Coastal Plan, involvement in the Army Corp of Engineers Sand Study, completed the five year update of the housing element update and now working on implemenatation of the housing development, as well as other projects such as the Special Commercial Zone development standards.
Angela Ivey, City Clerk, stated that the City Clerk’s office had completed refining public speaking limits to provid clarification for the public, that there had been 24 Council meetings as of this date, that there have been two Council seats up for election, and that there had been three elections within the past year. She stated that document imaging had been enhanced and there were twenty years of Ordinances, Minutes, and Resolutions that are scanned and easily searchable.
Chandra Collure, City Engineer, stated that the Engineering department had worked on projects such as the sewer forcemain, Cliff St. Bridge, Fletcher Cove park, that the Engineering department completed the South Granados Sewer construction project, had painted City Hall, and had installed a new Council dais.
Dennis Coleman, Finance Director, stated that the Finance department staff had worked on the Sewer Assessment financing, claims and litigation, and Redevelopement issues.
Dismas Ableman, Deputy Fire Chief, stated that the Code Enforcement department had a successful mediation this year, that the Fire department responded to 1,458 total responses, and provided education to homeowners and schools.
STAFF REPORTS: (Items 6-7)
Submit speaker slips to the City Clerk.
6.
Establishing the California Cities Coastal Cities Issue Group (CCIG) (File No. 0410-20)
A.
Appoint two Councilmembers to serve on the League of California Cities' Coastal Cities Issues Group (CCIG) and designate a Staff alternate.
Item 6 document
David Ott, City Manager, introduced the item and stated that the Council requested to participate in a new Council Regional Committee called the League of California Cities Coastal Issues Group to address coastal issues.
Council consensus to appoint Councilmember Roberts as the primary, Councilmember Kellejian as the alternate, and Leslea Meyerhoff as the Staff Consultant.
MOTION: Moved by Heebner and seconded by Campbell to appoint Councilmember Roberts as primary and Deputy Mayor Kellejian as the alternate and Leslea Meyerhoff, Consultant as the staff representative Motion carried unanimously.
7.
Substantial Conformance Request of a Previously Approved Conditional Use Permit, Development Review Permit and Structure Development Permit for development of property at 533 Lomas Santa Fe Drive (San Dieguito Boys & Girls Club; Case: 17-04-03 & 17-05-22 CUP/DRP/SDP and Continued from the March 14, 2007 Council Meeting) (File No. 0600-40)
Item 7 document
A.
Find the relocated rooftop condenser units in substantial conformance with the previously approved project.
David Ott, City Manager, introduced the item and stated that the Boys and Girls club requested to put condensor units on the roof of their building.
Kathy Johnson, Associate Planner, presented a powerpoint presentation on the project.
Keith Padget, Applicant, stated that the project was going well, that they were over budget, and that they were willing to look into plantings for around the project area.
MOTION: Moved by Roberts and seconded by Kellejian to approve Motion carried unanimously.
